If the person to whom any license under this article is issued does not personally manage the outlet, the name of each manager on duty at the outlet must always be registered with the city clerk, and each manager of the outlet shall meet all of the requirements of a person to whom a license could be granted hereunder. If such licensed outlet is not managed directly by the holder of the license, or a manager registered as provided hereunder who meets all of the requirements hereunder, then the license shall be immediately suspended or revoked. If such a manager is changed, the holder of the license must notify the city clerk not later than ten days from the date of the change of such manager and all information required hereunder with regard to managers shall also be furnished to the city clerk at such time. This section shall apply to any person who is in charge of the business operation of the outlet at any given time.
(Ord. of 2-3-86, § 3.22)
151:
All malt beverages and wine shall be located within the interior of the outlet and shall be sacked in containers at the check-out counter of such outlet, and no such beverages shall be opened or consumed either inside the outlet or on the premises of the outlet.
(Ord. of 2-3-86, § 3.16)
152:
At all times all retail licensees under this article must have within the place of business a copy of this article.
(Ord. of 2-3-86, § 3.14)
155:
(a) It shall be unlawful to manufacture, sell or offer to sell at wholesale or retail within the city any malt beverage without having the appropriate license for such manufacture or sale, or to carry on such activity in violation of the terms of such license or of this chapter.
(b) It shall be unlawful to sell, store or offer to sell at wholesale or retail within the city, wine without having the appropriate license for such sale or to carry on such activity in violation of the terms of such license or this chapter.
(Ord. of 2-3-86, §§ 1.2, 2.2)
156:
(a) A separate license shall be required for each malt beverage outlet and for each wine outlet, and separate application shall be made for each.
(b) No license shall be transferable or assignable.
(c) Immediately upon the sale of an outlet or immediately upon the closing of an outlet, it shall be the duty of the licensee to surrender his license to the city clerk.
(Ord. of 2-3-86, §§ 1.3, 2.3)
157:
No license granted under this article shall be transferable from one person to another, nor shall the same be transferable from one outlet (location) to another.
(Ord. of 2-3-86, § 3.21)
158:
Licenses under this article shall be classified as follows:
(1) Retail; convenience store means a retail store in which the primary function is the sale of food and related merchandise, and in which the sale of malt beverages and/or wine at retail is incidental to the operation thereof and in which the sales of malt beverages and/or wine constitute less than 50 percent of the gross sales of such store.
(2) Wholesale means wholesale malt beverage and/or wine distributors, who permit only the sale of malt beverages and/or wine at wholesale to duly licensed retailers.
(Ord. of 2-3-86, §§ 1.4, 2.4, 3.16)
159:
Application for retail or wholesale malt beverage license shall be as provided in this section:
(1) Each initial applicant shall make written application to the city for the privilege of engaging in the sale of malt beverages, specifying wholesale or retail, such application using forms approved by the governing body and furnished by the mayor.
(2) The application shall be filed with city clerk with a fee of $25.00 for investigation of the applicant and application and of the proposed location and processing of the application.
(3) The application shall state:
a. As to the applicant the full name, age, home address, telephone number, place of permanent residence, date of establishment of permanent residence at such location, address of last place of residence, name of spouse, complete record of all convictions, guilty pleas and pleas of nolo contendere for violation of all laws, city, state and federal, of applicant and of applicant's spouse. If the applicant is a partnership such information shall be furnished as to each partner. If the applicant is a corporation, such information must be furnished as to each director, each officer and each stockholder who owns or controls ten percent or more of the issued and outstanding stock of such corporation.
b. As to applicant's proposed outlet manager (if not same as applicant) the full name, age, home address, business address, telephone number, place of permanent residence, date of establishment at such location, address of last place of residence, name of spouse, complete record of all convictions, guilty pleas and pleas of nolo contendere for violation of all laws, city, state and federal, of the outlet manager and the outlet manager's spouse.
c. Exact location (street address and otherwise) of proposed business and outlet.
d. Name and address of owner or landlord and resident manager, if any, of property proposed for location and whether or not there is a building proposed to be used already erected thereon.
e. Name or trade name under which the proposed business shall be operated.
f. Name and address of all persons having any financial interest in the outlet by way of ownership of building or stock, receipt of income from business or otherwise. This shall not apply to any stockholder who owns less than ten percent of the issued and outstanding stock of the corporation.
g. If the applicant is a corporation, the address of the principal place of business, the registered office, and the name of the registered agents of the corporation.
h. Such other information as may be required by the city through interrogatories or otherwise.
(4) The application shall be sworn to by all applicants.
(5) There shall be attached to the application a copy of the applicant's application or proposed application for a license from the state if one is required.
(Ord. of 2-3-86, § 1.5)
160:
Application for a retail package wine license shall be the same as and in accordance with the requirements applicable to the sale of malt beverages by the package at retail, and all provisions in this chapter pertaining to the application and qualifications of a malt beverage licensee, including sections 6-43, 6-44, 6-46, 6-50 through 6-53 shall be enforced in the sale of wine.
(Ord. of 2-3-86, § 2.5)
161:
Within seven days from the time the application is filed, the mayor shall notify the police chief or such other investigative officer as approved by the city, who shall investigate the character of the applicant and the reputation of the location, and make a full report to the city. The mayor shall refer the application, together with any objections which may have been filed, to the city. The city shall, after investigation of applicant and proposed location, direct the city clerk to either refuse to issue a license, or to issue a license for which the application is made upon payment of the appropriate fee. The city shall either issue or refuse to issue the license for which application is made within 60 days from the time the application is filed.
(Ord. of 2-3-86, § 1.6)
162:
As a prerequisite to the issuance of any license hereunder, the applicant shall furnish a complete set of fingerprints which shall be forwarded to the Georgia Bureau of Investigation as is required under O.C.G.A. § 3-3-2(c).
(Ord. of 2-3-86, § 3.23)
163:
(a) The annual license fee for the privilege of engaging in the business of selling malt beverages at wholesale within the city shall be $50.00.
(b) The annual license fee for the privilege of engaging in business of selling wine at wholesale with the city shall be $50.00.
(c) The annual license fee for the privilege of engaging in the business of selling malt beverages at retail shall be $500.00.
(d) The annual license fee for the privilege of engaging in the business of selling wine at retail shall be $500.00.
(e) The annual license fee for engaging of selling wine and malt beverages of retail shall be $750.00.
(f) No license shall be issued for less than the calendar year as herein provided and in case of revocation or surrender of any such license before the expiration of such calendar year, the holder thereof shall not be entitled to receive any refund whatsoever.
(g) The aforesaid license fee herein set shall not be prorated for any portion of a year and shall remain the full amount regardless of the time the application is made.
(h) All license fees required under this article shall be paid prior to the issuance of any license.
(Ord. of 2-3-86, §§ 3.4, 3.17)
164:
All licenses required under this article shall be posted in a conspicuous place within the outlet. If the license is not so posted the outlet shall not be authorized to continue in business until the license is posted.
(Ord. of 2-3-86, § 3.13)
165:
(a) General. The city in making its determination on an initial application shall be guided by the factors set out in this section and section 6-51.
(b) Additional considerations. The city in reaching its final determination on an initial application shall also be guided by the following factors as to whether or not to grant such license:
(1) The proximity of other outlets.
(2) The nature of the neighborhood immediately adjacent to the proposed location; that is, whether the neighborhood is predominately residential, industrial or business.
(3) The proximity of public parks and playgrounds.
(4) Whether the proposed location has adequate off-street parking facilities or other parking available for its patrons.
(Ord. of 2-3-86, §§ 1.7, 1.8(4))
166:
(a) Prohibited location. It shall be unlawful to grant a license for the sale of malt beverages within the following areas in the city:
(1) Within a measured 200 feet of any hospital building or resthome building. The word "building" as used herein shall mean a structure used at the time of filing of the application of license for the purposes of a hospital or resthome.
(2) Within a measured 300 feet of any church property line. For the purposes of this article the words "church property" shall mean the premises upon which the main sanctuary is located. Additionally for the purpose of this article, a church is hereby defined as an organization for the purpose of preaching the gospel and other related religious activities located within a permanent structure either owned or leased by such organization or which is used by such organization with permission of the owner on a regular basis for such purpose. Such organization must either consist of 25 adult members on its official rolls that meet on a regularly scheduled basis not less than one time per week with an average attendance of not less than 25 people or such organization must be duly recognized and affiliated with a parent religious denomination and be either charted, recognized or approved by the parent religious denomination. Such organization must qualify under the rule of the internal revenue service as an organization to which contributions may be deducted for federal income tax purposes.
(3) Within 300 feet, measured in a straight line, from the nearest property line of any school or school house to the nearest corner of the building which the outlet or proposed outlet is to be operated.
(4) In any existing building or establishment having a history or reputation for prostitution or other sex offenses; fighting, shooting, stabbing or other violence; gambling; illegal dealing in alcoholic beverages or drugs; or other violations of the law.
(b) Prohibited outlet building. It shall be unlawful to grant a license for the sale of malt beverages at retail where the proposed location does not have a front entrance to the premises which is clearly visible from a public street, road or highway.
(c) Prohibited persons. It shall be unlawful to grant a license for the sale of malt beverages to:
(1) A person who is not a citizen of the United States.
(2) A corporation which is not duly qualified to do business in the State of Georgia and which is not in good standing with all of the rules and regulations of the Georgia Corporation Code and the secretary of state, and which does not have a registered agent for service of process within the state; however, the provisions of this subsection shall not apply to an individual or a partnership which has no corporate partners.
(3) A person who is not of good character and reputation in the community in which he resides.
(4) A person who has been convicted of a felony, or of a crime opposed to decency and morality, within ten years immediately prior to the filing of the application.
(5) A person who has been convicted or who has entered a plea of nolo contendere for any felony or any misdemeanor involving the illegal possession, transportation or sale of any alcoholic spirits, prohibited liquors, wines or malt beverages, or taxability thereof within ten years immediately prior to the filing of the application.
(6) A person who has been convicted or who has entered a plea of nolo contendere for any felony or any misdemeanor involving the illegal possession, transportation or sale of any drug, narcotic or controlled substance within ten years immediately prior to the filing of the application.
(7) A person, partnership or corporation whose license under this article has been revoked for cause or who has had a license of any type under this article revoked for cause within five years immediately prior to the filing of the application.
(8) A person, partnership or corporation who at the time of application for renewal of any license issued hereunder would not be eligible for such license upon a first application.
(9) A person who is under the age of 21 years.
(10) A person who is not of sound mind and memory.
(11) An elected official or police officer or other law enforcement officer of the city.
(12) If the applicant is a corporation, subsections (c)(3), (4), (5), (6), (9) and (10) of this section shall not apply.
(13) Any partnership or corporation where any individual having any interest, either as owner, partner, stockholder, director or officer, or his or her spouse, shall have been convicted or shall have entered a plea of nolo contendere for any felony, or a crime opposed to decency and morality, or any felony or misdemeanor involving the manufacturing, possession, transportation or sale of beer, alcoholic spirits, wine, or prohibited liquors, or the taxability thereof, or a violation of this chapter, or shall have been convicted or shall have entered a plea of nolo contendere for any felony or misdemeanor involving the illegal possession, transportation or sale of any drug, narcotic or controlled substance within ten years immediately prior to the filing of such application.
(Ord. of 2-3-86, § 1.8(1)-(3))
167:
(a) All licenses shall be issued for a period of one calendar year, running from January 1 through December 31, and shall be renewable as a matter of course upon payment of the appropriate fee except as set out in subsection (d) of this section.
(b) Each licensee shall make written application for renewal on or before December 1 of each year on forms approved by the mayor.
(c) Such application shall be referred to the police chief or such other person as is designated by the city, who shall report on the licensee's activity, if any, and upon activity at the location of the licensed business, if any, during the year.
(d) If the police chief or designated investigator reports any activity which constitutes probable cause for not renewing a license, the renewal shall not be made, and the matter shall be referred to the city for its consideration. A public hearing must be held not later than December 31.
(e) The city shall afford the licensee a public hearing and in passing upon the application for renewal, it shall be guided by the following factors applicable to an initial application: All matters contained in sections 6-50 and 6-51 and such evidence as is obtained and presented to the city as the result of the investigation provided for in subsection (c) of this section. The city shall consider all evidence presented at the public hearing.
(f) At the public hearing the city may grant or deny for cause the renewal of any license issued hereunder.
(Ord. of 2-3-86, § 1.9)
168:
(a) Summary action.
(1) If, at any time during the holding of a license granted under this article, it should appear that the licensee has violated the provisions of this chapter, or the state or federal laws relating to the possession, transportation or sale of any alcoholic spirits, prohibited liquors, wine or malt beverages or taxability thereof or involving the illegal possession, transportation or sale of any drug, narcotic or controlled substance, or has become a person prohibited by this chapter from having a license granted to him or her, as contained in sections 6-50 and 6-51, or if it should appear that the application contained known false information, or if it appears necessary for the public safety, health and welfare, the chief of police or some other police officer directed by the city may suspend and seize any retail license to sell malt beverages within the city.
(2) If the licensee is dissatisfied with such suspension, such licensee may appeal to the city by filing a written request with the city clerk stating the grounds and reasons.
(3) The city shall hold a hearing on such suspension within ten days of the filing of such appeal. After such hearing, the city may affirm, reverse or modify the action of the suspending officer and may revoke or suspend the license or place the licensee on probation or refuse to renew at the time of renewal.
(b) Action by city. The city shall have full power to revoke, refuse to renew, suspend or place on probation any license to sell malt beverages for violation of this chapter or violation of any law of the state or any federal law involving possession, transportation or sale of any alcoholic spirits, prohibited liquors, wine or malt beverages or taxability thereof or involving any illegal possession, transportation or sale of any drug, narcotic or controlled substance, or if the licensee has become a person prohibited by this chapter from having a license granted to such person or it, as contained in sections 6-50 and 6-51, or if it should appear that the application contained known false information, or when the city shall determine after five days' notice and hearing that the operation of the licensed business is detrimental to the health, safety or welfare of the public. For the purposes of this section it shall be sufficient if notice is mailed giving the time and place of the hearing by United States registered or certified mail at the address of the licensee shown in the application.
(Ord. of 2-3-86, § 1.10)
169:
In addition to the license required by the city, each licensee must obtain any permit or license required by the state and/or the United States of America. Failure to obtain any such license or permit or the revocation of any such license or permit shall be grounds for suspension or revocation of a license granted under this article.
(Ord. of 2-3-86, § 3.23)
172:
It shall be unlawful for any person to sell at retail or other vise within the city any malt beverage or wine on which the tax required in this division has not been paid to the wholesaler or distributor or to the city.
(Ord. of 2-3-86, § 1.16)
173:
The failure to make a timely report and remit the taxes levied herein shall render a wholesale dealer liable for a penalty equal to ten percent of the total amount due in addition to the amount due; and, additionally, if the report is not filed or if the taxes are not remitted and paid within 30 days from the date the taxes are due, the city shall have the right to suspend and/or revoke any wholesale license and further to prohibit such wholesaler from making any deliveries of any type whatsoever within the corporate limits of the city.
(Ord. of 2-3-86, § 1.15)
174:
In addition to the annual license fee required, there is hereby levied and imposed an excise tax which shall be paid to the city, on all malt beverages which are sold within the corporate limits of the city. Such excise tax is to be that amount authorized in O.C.G.A. § 3-5-80. Such excise tax is imposed upon and shall be paid by each wholesale dealer who sells and/or delivers malt beverages within the corporate limits of the city.
(Ord. of 2-3-86, § 1.11)
175:
Such tax shall be paid to the city by each wholesale dealer on all malt beverages sold and/or delivered within the corporate limits of the city not later than the tenth day of each month, based upon the units of beverage sold during the previous calendar month by such wholesalers to retailers in the city.
(Ord. of 2-3-86, § 1.12)
176:
The wholesale dealer shall keep true and correct records of all sales and shipments and shall render a sworn statement of the same accompanying the monthly report to the city. Such report shall show the exact quantities of malt beverages by size and type of container and the amount of excise tax collected.
(Ord. of 2-3-86, § 1.13)
177:
The city shall have the right to audit and to require production of records from each wholesaler supplying retailers in the city and also from each retailer so supplied within the city.
(Ord. of 2-3-86, § 1.14)
178:
In addition to the annual retail wine license fee required, there is hereby levied an excise tax computed as follows: $0.20 per liter and a proportionate tax at a rate of $0.20 per liter on all fractional parts of a liter and an additional tax at the same rate on all fractions above a liter.
(Ord. of 2-3-86, § 2.6(a))
State Law reference— Authority, O.C.G.A. § 3-6-60.
179:
The excise tax on wine shall be paid to the city by each wholesale distributor on all wine sold to retailers in the city not later than the tenth day of each month, based upon the units of wine sold during the previous calendar month by such wholesalers to retailers in the city.
(Ord. of 2-3-86, § 2.6(b))
180:
(a) Each wholesale distributor shall furnish the city a summary of all purchase invoices for wine sold to each retailer in the city on or before the tenth day of each month following such purchases. Such invoices shall show the exact quantities of wine by size and type of container, and the amount of excise tax paid and the amount of excise tax collected.
(b) All the foregoing reports herein required shall be under oath.
(Ord. of 2-3-86, § 2.6(c), (e))
181:
The city shall have the right to audit, and the right to require production of records from each wholesaler who supplies retailers in the city and from each retailer supplied.
(Ord. of 2-3-86, § 2.6(d))
185:
This article shall be known as the "City of Trenton Malt Beverage/Wine by the Drink Ordinance."
(Ord. No. 10/01, § 1, 11-01-10)
186:
General prohibition: No person shall sell malt beverages or wine by the drink as provided for in this article without first obtaining all applicable licenses required by this article, and further:
(a) Malt beverages and wine may be sold for the limited purposes described herein within the the city under a license granted by the city upon the terms and conditions provided in this article.
(b) All licenses pursuant to this article shall be a mere grant of privilege to carry on the business during the term of the license, subject to all terms and conditions imposed by this article and state law.
(c) Any holder of a license issued in accord with this article is required to apply for and obtain an alcoholic beverage license from the State of Georgia before any sales commence. Additionally, any holder of a license issued in accord with this article is required to abide by all applicable state regulations and laws.
(d) All licenses issued under this chapter shall have printed on the face the following words: THIS LICENSE IS A PRIVILEGE CONDITIONAL ON THE HOLDER MEETING ALL STANDARDS FOR SUCH LICENSE AND OPERATING REGULATIONS APPLICABLE THERETO SET OUT IN CITY ORDINANCES AND GEORGIA LAW. FAILURE TO MEET SUCH STANDARDS OR TO COMPLY WITH SUCH OPERATING REGULATIONS SHALL SUBJECT THE HOLDER OF THE LICENSE TO HAVE THE LICENSE REVOKED FOLLOWING NOTICE AND HEARING.
(Ord. No. 10/01, § 2, 11-01-10)
187:
The following words, terms, and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed in this section, except if the context clearly indicates a different meaning, to-wit:
(a) Alcohol means malt beverage and wine.
(b) Beer or malt beverage means any alcoholic beverage obtained by the fermentation of any infusion or decoction of barley, malt, hops or any other product, or any combination of such products in water containing no more than six percent alcohol by volume and including, but not limited to, ale, porter, brown stout, lager beer, small beer, and strong beer. The term "malt beverage" does not include sake, known as Japanese rice wine.
(c) Eating establishment means any public place, including a place available for rental by the public, selling prepared food for consumption by the public on the premises with a full service kitchen. A full service kitchen shall consist of a three-compartment pot sink, a stove or grill permanently installed, and refrigerator, all of which must be approved by the health and fire departments. An eating establishment shall be prepared to serve food every hour the establishment is open and shall derive at least 70 percent of the gross receipts annually from the sale of prepared meals or food.
(d) Hotel/motel means any building or other structure providing sleeping accommodations for hire to the general public, either transient, permanent or residential. Such businesses shall have one or more public dining rooms with a full service kitchen, as that term is defined in subsection (c). Hotels/motels shall have the privilege of granting franchises for the operation of any licensed establishment described in this article, and the holder of such franchise shall be included in the definition of a hotel/motel pursuant to this definition.
(e) Licensee means the person to whom a license for the sale or distribution of malt beverages or wine is issued under this article. In the case of a partnership or corporation, all partners, officers, and directors of the partnership or corporation are licensees. A license issued under this article permits the licensee to sell malt beverages and/or wine for beverage purposes by the drink for consumption only on the premises where sold.
(f) Person means any individual, firm, partnership, cooperative, nonprofit membership corporation, joint venture, association, company, corporation, agency, syndicate, estate, trust, business trust, receiver, fiduciary, or other group or combination acting as a unit, body politic, or political subdivision, whether public, private, or quasi-public.
(g) Premises means one room or more all contiguous in nature operating under the same trade name.
(h) Retail consumption dealer means any person who sells malt beverages or wine for consumption on the premises, at retail, only to consumers and not for resale.
(i) Wine means any alcoholic beverage containing not more that 21 percent alcohol made from fruits, berries, or grapes either by natural fermentation or by natural fermentation with brandy added. Wine includes, but is not limited to, all sparkling wines, champagnes, combinations of such beverages, vermouths, special natural wines, rectified wines, and like products. The term "wine" does not include cooking wine mixed with salt or other ingredients so as to render it unfit for human consumption as a beverage. A liquid shall first be deemed to be a wine at the point in the manufacturing process when it conforms to the definition of wine contained in this section.
(Ord. No. 10/01, § 3, 11-01-10)
189:
Only the following licenses shall be issued under this article:
(1) Malt beverages by the drink for consumption on the premises;
(2) Wine by the drink for consumption on the premises; and
(3) Malt beverages and wine by the drink for consumption on the premises.
(Ord. No. 10/01, § 5, 11-01-10)
190:
It shall be unlawful for any person to sell or possess for the purpose of sale any malt beverage or wine if the person does not have a license granted by the city to sell or possess for sale malt beverage or wine or to make deliveries beyond the boundaries of the premises covered by the license. Violations of this section shall be dealt with pursuant to section 6-26 hereof.
(Ord. No. 10/01, § 6, 11-01-10)
191:
Any violation of the provisions of this article may upon determination of violation result in suspension or revocation of a license issued pursuant to this article; or the commission may in lieu of suspension or revocation thereof impose a civil penalty of not less than $500.00 nor more than $1,000.00.
(Ord. No. 10/01, § 7, 11-01-10)
192:
(a) No malt beverage or wine shall be sold for consumption on the premises where sold except in all areas zoned Business and which are being used as one of the following:
(1) An eating establishment, as that term is defined in section 6-22(c) hereof. When eating establishments are located in hotels or motels, every entrance to the establishment shall be from a public lobby, hallway, mall or other publicly used interior portion of the primary use structure; or
(2) An indoor nonprofit civic and cultural center qualified under section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code capable of serving prepared food, with a full service kitchen, as that term is defined in section 6-22(c); prepared to serve food every hour they are open and deriving at least 70 percent of its total annual gross sales from the sale of prepared meals or foods and recreation activities.
These eating establishments must be located in a zoning district which permits restaurants as conforming uses or where these eating establishments are incidental to a hotel or motel.
(b) No license will be issued for the retail sale of malt beverages and/or wine for consumption on the premises within 100 yards of schools, alcohol treatment centers, or the city recreation property with the exception of the city's civic center. Said distance shall be measured in a straight line from the nearest property line of any school, alcohol treatment center, or the city recreation property to the nearest corner of the building where the malt beverage and/or wine is to be sold by the drink for consumption on the premises.
(Ord. No. 10/01, § 8, 11-01-10)
193:
Separate applications must be made for each location and separate licenses must be issued for each location.
(Ord. No. 10/01, § 9, 11-01-10; Ord. No. 15/03, § 1, 5-15-15)
194:
(a) The fees for licenses issued pursuant to this article are as follows:
(1) Retail dealer of malt beverage to be consumed on the premises $500.00 per calendar year;
(2) Retail dealer of wine to be consumed on the premises $500.00 per calendar year;
(3) Retail dealer of malt beverage and wine to be consumed on the premises $1,000.00 per calendar year. The license fee shall not be prorated based upon the day of the year that the license is issued.
(b) Each application for a license under this article shall be accompanied by a certified check for the full amount of the appropriate license fee, together with a separate check or cash in the amount of $150.00 to defray investigative and administrative costs. If the application is denied and the license refused, or if the applicant withdraws his application prior to the license being issued, the license fee shall be refunded, but the $150.00 cost paid for investigative and administrative fees shall be retained by the city. However, any person applying for more than one license at the same time shall pay only one fee to defray investigative and administrative expenses. Any applicant for a license under this article who has in existence at the time of making the new application an existing license under this article shall pay no investigative and administrative fee. A notice of each application to sell malt beverages and/or wine by consumption shall be advertised in the official legal organ of Dade County, once a week for two weeks immediately preceding consideration of the application.
(c) Once a license has been issued, however, no portion of the license fee shall be refunded if the license is revoked, suspended, or surrendered.
(Ord. No. 10/01, § 10, 11-01-10)
195:
(a) Malt beverages and/or wine shall not be sold or distributed for consumption on the premises except Monday through Saturday between the hours of 10:00 a.m. through 12:00 midnight.
(b) Sunday sales: The sale or distribution of beer and/or wine for consumption on the premises shall not be permitted on Sundays.
(c) Election Day sales: The sale of malt beverage and/or wine under this article shall be prohibited on election days within the city during the hours the polls are open.
(d) Christmas Day sales: The sale or distribution of beer and/or wine for consumption on the premises shall not be permitted on Christmas Day.
(Ord. No. 10/01, § 11, 11-01-10)
196:
No person shall allow or require a person in his employment under 18 years of age to dispense, serve, sell, or take orders for any malt beverage or wine.
(Ord. No. 10/01, § 12, 11-01-10)
197:
It shall be a violation of this article not to require and properly check identification for such persons as reasonably necessary to ensure that an underage person is not sold, served, or does not have in his possession malt beverage or wine while in a licensed establishment. Identification in this section shall mean any document issued by a governmental agency containing a description of the person, such person's photograph and giving such person's date of birth and shall include, without being limited to, a passport, military ID card, driver's license or state department of public safety ID card. Nothing herein shall require mandatory checking of all customers' identifications.
(Ord. No. 10/01, § 13, 11-01-10)
198:
It is prohibited for any person to bring his own malt beverage and/or wine in any establishment either licensed or unlicensed to serve malt beverage and/or wine.
(Ord. No. 10/01, § 14, 11-01-10)
199:
The city license issued pursuant to this article shall at all times be kept plainly exposed to view to the public at the place of business of the licensee.
(Ord. No. 10/01, § 15, 11-01-10)
200:
There shall be no transfers of licenses. Any change in ownership of any licensed entity other than a publicly traded corporation shall necessitate a new application and payment of the entirety of the license fee and administrative fee.
(Ord. No. 10/01, § 16, 11-01-10)
201:
No licensee under this article shall keep any malt beverage or wine at any place except the licensed place of business.
(Ord. No. 10/01, § 17, 11-01-10)
202:
For purposes of this article, notice shall be deemed delivered when personally served or when served by certified mail, within three days after the date of the deposit in the United States Mail; or the date of confirmation of delivery from an overnight delivery service.
(Ord. No. 10/01, § 18, 11-01-10)
205:
Poured malt beverages or wine shall be transported from point of dispensing to the customer by permitted employees only. Permitted employees are those who have applied for and received a pouring license authorizing such employees to take orders and transport alcoholic beverages to customers.
(Ord. No. 10/01, § 19, 11-01-10)
206:
The following regulations shall apply to all establishments holding a license for consumption of malt beverages and/or wine on the premises:
(1) No person shall be employed to dispense malt beverages or wine or serve in any managerial position by an establishment holding a license under this article until such person has been fingerprinted and cleared by the chief of police for the city or his designee and/or city code enforcement officer indicating that the person is eligible for such employment as per the minimum requirements for an applicant under this article.
(2) This section shall not be construed to include employees whose duties are limited solely to those of busboy(s), cooks, or dishwashers.
(3) No permit shall be issued until such time as a signed application has been filed with the city clerk or designee and upon payment of a fee in the amount of $50.00 and a search of the criminal record of the applicant completed. The application shall include, but shall be limited to, the name, date of birth and prior arrest record of the person, though the fact of an arrest record shall be used for investigative purposes only, and shall give rise to no presumption or inference of guilt. Due to the inclusion of the arrest information, the application shall be regarded as confidential and shall not be produced for public inspection without a court order.
(4) The city clerk or a designee shall have a complete and exhaustive search made relative to any criminal record of the person fingerprinted. If the person is eligible for employment, the city clerk or a designee shall issue a permit to the person, by mail, stating that the person is eligible for employment. If it is found that the person is not eligible for employment, the chief of police or city code enforcement officer or other designee shall notify the person, in writing, that he or she is not eligible for employment, the cause of such denial and his or her right of appeal.
(5) No person shall be granted a pouring permit unless it appears to the satisfaction of the city clerk or a designee that such person has not been convicted or pled guilty or entered a plea of nolo contendere to any crime involving moral turpitude, illegal gambling, illegal possession or sale of controlled substances or the illegal sale or possession of alcoholic beverages, including the sale or transfer of alcoholic beverages to a minor in a manner contrary to law, keeping a place of prostitution, solicitation of sodomy, or any sexually related crime within a period of five years preceding the date of the application and is not on probation or parole. A person's first time conviction for illegal possession of alcohol as a misdemeanor or violation of a city or county ordinance shall not, by itself, make a person ineligible for an alcohol pouring permit. No person shall be granted a pouring permit who has been convicted, plead guilty or entered a plea of nolo contendere to any federal, state, or local law for any felony within five years preceding the date of the application and is currently on probation or parole. For purposes of this article, a conviction or pleas of guilt or nolo contendere shall be ignored as to any offense for which a person whose sentence was entered under the Georgia First Offender Act, as amended. Except, however, that any such offense shall not be ignored if the person violated any term of probation imposed by the court granting first offender treatment or committed another crime and the sentencing court entered an adjudication of guilt as to the crime for which the person had previously been sentenced as a first offender.
(6) An alcohol pouring permit shall be issued for a period of three calendar years from the date of the application. As provided in subsection (11), the alcohol pouring permit must be in the possession of the employee while the employee is working at the licensed establishment and available for inspection by members of the city police department. After application of the pouring permit is completed with the city, the employee may immediately commence work on a temporary basis provided the employee retains the receipt for the permit on his or her person at all times at the premises for which the alcohol license has been issued, and thereafter, if a permit is issued, must maintain on his or her person at the premises the actual pouring permit. If a permit is not issued, the employee must immediately cease work upon being notified that a permit will not be issued to the employee.
(7) No person shall be issued a permit if it is determined that the person falsified, concealed or covered up any material fact by any device, trick or scheme while making application to the city clerk for an alcohol beverage pouring permit under this section. If it is determined that a person is in violation of this subsection and a permit is denied for this reason, then 90 calendar days must elapse from the date of notification of the denial of the permit before the person may submit a new application for a permit.
(8) All permits issued through administrative error can be immediately terminated and seized by the city clerk or designee.
(9) Replacement permits will be issued within 30 days of original date, upon paying one-half of the fee charged for alcohol pouring permits. After 30 days of original application date, a new application and fee must be submitted.
(10) All permits issued under this article remain the property of the city and shall be produced for inspection upon the demand of any city police officer, city code enforcement officer, city clerk or a designee.
(11) No licensee shall allow any employee or manager required to hold a permit to work on premises unless the employee or manager has in his or her possession a current valid city pouring permit. For new employees, a receipt issued by the city clerk may be used for a maximum of 90 days from the date of its issue unless notified that a permit will not be issued. Licensees are required by this article to inspect and verify that each employee required to do so has in his or her possession a valid current alcohol pouring permit.
(12) It shall be the duty of all persons holding any license issued under this article to file with the city clerk the name of the establishment, the license number and a list of all employees, with their home addresses and home telephone numbers, twice annually during the month of June and again during the month of December.
(13) The permit issued under this section shall be issued to individuals only and as long as the permit is valid, may be used at any employer licensed by this article until said license is revoked, suspended, terminated, or expires.
(Ord. No. 03-03, § 3, 12-1-03; Ord. No. 10/01, § 20, 11-01-10)
207:
(a) Alcoholic beverage sales can be made by a licensed consumption on premises establishment in a patio/open area type environment if the establishment has been approved to do so by the code enforcement officer and is in compliance with any and all other regulations of the city. Also, all sales of malt beverages and wine under this provision must be in opaque containers and not in bottles or cans.
(b) The requirement for approval is that the patio/open area be enclosed by some structure providing for public ingress/egress only through the main licensed premises. The purpose of this requirement is to prevent a customer from leaving the outside sales area with an open drink without the licensee's knowledge.
(c) The height of such structure shall be a minimum of three and one-half feet above the patio floor, but the structure does have to shield or restrict visibility into or out of the patio/open sales area. The structure must be permitted and approved by the code enforcement officer and meet all building and fire code regulations.
(d) The only exit from the patio/open sales area is to be through the licensed establishment's main premises and through an approved fire exit, not for general public use unless an emergency exists. The fire exit must be of a type that sounds an alarm so that the establishment will be alerted in the event of unauthorized use when no emergency exists.
(Ord. No. 10/01, § 21, 11-01-10)
208:

(b) It is prohibited for customers to gather outside a malt beverage and/or wine establishment and consume malt beverage and/or wine.

(Ord. No. 10/01, § 22, 11-01-10)

213:
(1) In addition to the license fees required in this article and in addition to the excise taxes levied by the state, there is hereby imposed an excise tax on alcoholic beverages in the following amounts:
a. Where malt beverages, commonly known as tap or draft beer, are sold in or from a barrel or bulk container, a tax of $6.00 on each container sold containing not more than 15½ gallons and a proportionate tax at the same rate on all fractional parts of 15½ gallons.

(Ord. No. 10/01, § 26, 11-01-10)

220:
(a) Application for the sale of malt beverages and/or wine for consumption on the premises license shall be as follows: Each initial applicant shall make written application to the city clerk or a designee for the privilege of engaging in the sale of malt beverages for consumption on the premises; using forms approved and furnished by the city clerk.
(1) The application shall be filed with the city clerk with a fee of $150.00 for investigation of the application and of the proposed location and processing of the application.
(2) The application shall state:
a. As to the applicant: Full name, age, home address, business address, telephone number, place of permanent residence, date of establishment of permanent residence at said location, address of last place of residence, name of spouse and all minor children, complete record of all convictions, guilty pleas and pleas of nolo contendere for violation of all laws, city, state and federal, of applicant and of applicant's spouse. If the applicant is a partnership said information shall be furnished as to each partner. If the applicant is a corporation said information must be furnished as to each director, each officer, and each stockholder who owns or controls ten percent or more of the issued and outstanding stock of said corporation.
b. As to applicant's proposed establishment manager or managers (if not same as applicant): Full name, age, home address, business address, telephone number, place of permanent residence, date of establishment of permanent residence at said location, address of last place of residence, name of spouse and all minor children, complete record of all convictions, guilty pleas and pleas of nolo contendere for violation of all laws, city, state and federal, of outlet manager's spouse.
c. Exact location (street address) of proposed business establishment.
d. Name and address of owner or landlord and resident manager, if any, of property proposed for location and whether or not there is a building proposed to be used already erected thereon.
e. Name or trade name under which the proposed business shall be operated.
f. Name and address of all persons having any financial interest in the business by way of ownership of building or stock, receipt of income from business or otherwise. This shall not apply to any stockholder who owns less than ten percent of the issued and outstanding stock of the corporation.
g. If the applicant is a corporation, the address of the principal place of business, the registered office, and the name of the registered agent or agents of the corporation.
h. Such other information as may be required from time to time by the city through interrogatories or otherwise.
(3) The application shall be sworn to by all applicants.
(4) There shall be attached to the application a copy of applicant's license, application for license, or proposed application for a license from the State of Georgia, if one be required.
(b) Prohibited premises. It shall be unlawful to grant a license for the sale of malt beverages and/or wine for consumption on the premises where the proposed location does not have a front entrance to the premises which is clearly visible from a public street, road or highway.
(c) Prohibited persons. It shall be unlawful to grant a license for the sale of malt beverages and/or wine for consumption on the premises to:
a. A person who is not a citizen of the United States for a period of 12 months next preceding the date of filing of the application, and if the applicant is a partnership these requirements apply to all partners in said business, whether a general partner or a limited partner; however, the provisions of this subsection shall not apply to a corporation.
b. A corporation which is not duly qualified to do business in the State of Georgia and which is not in good standing with all of the rules and regulations of the Georgia Corporation Code and the Secretary of State of Georgia, and which does not have a registered agent for service of process within Dade County, Georgia; however, the provisions of this sub-paragraph shall not apply to an individual or a partnership which has no corporate partners.
c. A person who has been convicted of a felony, or any crime of moral turpitude, within ten years immediately prior to the filing of said application.
d. A person who has been convicted or who has entered a plea of guilty or nolo contendere for any felony or any misdemeanor involving the illegal possession, transportation or sale of any alcoholic spirits, prohibited liquors, wine or malt beverages, or taxability thereof within ten years immediately prior to the filing of said application.
e. A person who has been convicted or who has entered a plea of guilty or nolo contendere for any felony or any misdemeanor involving the illegal possession, transportation or sale of any drug, narcotic or controlled substance within ten years immediately prior to the filing of said application.
f. A person, partnership or corporation whose license under this article has been revoked for cause or who has had a license of any type under this article revoked for cause within five years immediately prior to the filing of the application.
g. A person who is under the age of twenty-one years.
h. A person who has been declared incompetent by a court of competent jurisdiction.
i. An elected official or police officer or other law enforcement officer of the City of Trenton, Georgia.
j. If the applicant is a corporation, subsections c, d, e, g, h and i above shall not apply.
k. Any partnership or corporation where any individual having any interest, either as owner, partner, stockholder, director or officer, or his or her spouse, shall have been convicted or shall have entered a plea of guilty or nolo contendere within ten years immediately prior to the filing of said application of any felony, or any crime of moral turpitude, or any felony or misdemeanor involving the manufacturing, possession, transportation or sale of beer, alcoholic spirits, wine, or prohibited liquors, or the taxability thereof, or a violation of this article, or shall have been convicted or shall have entered a plea of guilty or nolo contendere within ten years immediately prior to the filing of said application for any felony or misdemeanor involving the illegal possession, transportation or sale of any drug, narcotic or controlled substance.
(d) Additional considerations. The city in reaching its final determination on an initial application shall also be guided by following factors as to whether or not to grant such license:
a. The proximity of other establishments licensed hereunder.
b. The nature of the neighborhood immediately adjacent to the proposed location, that is, whether the same is predominantly residential, industrial or business.
c. Whether the proposed location has adequate off-street parking facilities or other parking available for its patrons.
(Ord. No. 10/01, § 29, 11-01-10)
221:
(a) All licenses shall be issued for a period of one year, the same to be a calendar year, running from January 1 through December 31, and shall be renewable as a matter of course upon payment of the appropriate fee, except as is hereinafter set out in subsection (d) hereof and as otherwise provided in this article.

222:
(1) Summary action.
(a) If, at any time during the holding of a license granted under this article, it should appear that the licensee has violated the provisions of this article or laws of the State of Georgia or federal laws relating to the possession, transportation or sale of any alcohol, alcoholic spirits, prohibited liquors, wine or malt beverages or taxability thereof or involving the illegal possession, transportation or sale of any drug, narcotic or controlled substance, or has become a person prohibited by this article from having a license granted to him, or if it should appear that said person's application contained known false information, or if it appears necessary for the public safety, health and welfare, the chief of police, code enforcement officer or a designee may suspend and seize any retail license to sell malt beverages and wine within the city.
(b) If the licensee is dissatisfied with such suspension, he may appeal to the city commission by filing a written request with the city clerk stating his grounds and reasons.
(c) The city commission shall hold a hearing on such suspension within ten days of the filing of such appeal. After such hearing, the city commission may affirm, reverse or modify the action of the suspending officer and may revoke or suspend said license or place said licensee on probation or refuse to renew at the time of renewal.
(2) Action by city. The city commission shall have full power and authority to revoke, refuse to renew, suspend or place on probation any license to sell malt beverages and/or wine for consumption on the premises for violation of this article or violation of any laws of the State of Georgia or any federal laws involving possession, transportation or sale of any alcohol, alcoholic spirits, prohibited liquors, wine or malt beverages or taxability thereof or involving illegal possession, transportation or sale of any drug, narcotic or controlled substance, or if the licensee has become a person, firm or corporation prohibited by this article from having a license granted to him or it, or if it should appear that his application contained known false information, or when the city commission shall determine, after notice and hearing, that the operation of the licensed business is detrimental to the health, safety or welfare of the public.
(3) Hearings.
(a) Except as provided in subsection (1)(a) of this section, no license shall be suspended, revoked or non-renewed without the opportunity for a hearing as provided herein.
(b) The city commission or its designee shall provide written notice to the licensee of its intent to suspend, revoke or not renew the license. Such written notification shall be given as provided in this article. The notice shall:
(1) Advise of the time and place specified for the hearing, which hearing shall be held not more than fifteen days, but not less than ten days from the date notice is given, as provided herein;
(2) Shall set forth in reasonable detail the ground or grounds for such action and the factual basis supporting the ground or grounds; and
(3) Advise the licensee of the right to present evidence, witnesses, and arguments and to be represented by counsel at the hearing.
(4) The city commission shall make its final determination within ten business days of the completion of the hearing.
(5) The city commission's decision shall be personally served or mailed by certified mail, return receipt requested to the licensee and his attorney, with a copy to the city attorney, within ten business days of the close of the hearing. The decision of the city commission shall constitute final action by the city, subject to review upon petition for certiorari to the Superior Court of Dade County, Georgia.
(c) Upon receipt of notice of adverse action against the licensee under this section, the licensee may waive its right to a hearing and stipulate to a sanction, as recommended by the city clerk in consultation with the chief of police. Any stipulation entered under this subsection shall be in writing, signed by the licensee, and is nonappealable.
(Ord. No. 10/01, § 31, 11-01-10)
227:
Unless the context clearly indicates a different meaning, the following words, terms, and phrases, when used in this division, have the following meanings:
Date of notice means the date when a person is personally served with a written document or three days after the date of the deposit in the United States Mail when the document is served by certified mail; or the date of confirmation of delivery of the written document from an overnight delivery service.
Distilled spirits means any alcoholic beverage obtained by distillation or containing more than 24 percent alcohol by volume.
Eating establishment means any public place, including a place available for rental by the public, selling prepared food for consumption by the public on the premises with a full-service kitchen. A full-service kitchen shall consist of a three-compartment pot sink, a stove or grill permanently installed, and refrigerator, all of which must be approved by the health and fire departments. An eating establishment shall be prepared to serve food every hour the establishment is open and shall derive at least 70 percent of the gross receipts annually from the sale of prepared meals or food.
Hotel/motel means any building or other structure providing sleeping accommodations for hire to the general public, either transient, permanent or residential. Such businesses shall have one or more public dining rooms with a full-service kitchen, as that term is defined in [previous term]. Hotels/motels shall have the privilege of granting franchises for the operation of any licensed establishment described in this division, and the holder of such franchise shall be included in the definition of a hotel/motel pursuant to this definition.
Identification means any document issued by a governmental agency containing a description of the person, such person's photograph and giving such person's date of birth and shall include, without being limited to, a passport, military ID card, driver's license or state department of public safety ID card.
Licensee means the person to whom a license for the sale or distribution of distilled spirits is issued under this division. In the case of a partnership or corporation, all partners, officers, and directors of the partnership or corporation are licensees. A license issued under this division permits the licensee to sell distilled spirits for beverage purposes by the drink for consumption only on the premises where sold.
Person means any individual, firm, partnership, cooperative, nonprofit membership corporation, joint venture, association, company, corporation, agency, syndicate, estate, trust, business trust, receiver, fiduciary, or other group or combination acting as a unit, body politic, or political subdivision, whether public, private, or quasi-public.
Premises means one room or more all contiguous in nature operating under the same trade name.
Retail consumption dealer means any person who sells distilled spirits for consumption on the premises, at retail, only to consumers and not for resale.
Wholesaler means any person who sells distilled spirits to other wholesale dealers or to a retail consumption dealer.
(Ord. of 12-10-18(1))

(a) License suspensions initiated by the chief of police, code enforcement officer, or a designee.

(i) Violated the provisions of this division;
(ii) Violated any laws of the State of Georgia or any Federal laws involving possession, transportation or sale of any alcohol, alcoholic spirits, prohibited liquors, alcoholic beverages or taxability thereof or involving illegal possession, transportation or sale of any drug, narcotic or controlled substance;
(iii) Become a person, firm or corporation prohibited by this division from having a license granted to him, her, or it;
(iv) Submitted an application containing known false information; or
(v) Engaged in conduct detriment to the health, safety, or welfare of the public.
(2) If the licensee is dissatisfied with such suspension, the licensee may appeal to the city commission by filing a written request with the city clerk stating the grounds and reasons.
(3) The city commission will hold a hearing on the suspension within ten days of the filing of the appeal, after which the city commission has the full authority and power to revoke, refuse to renew, further suspend, or place on probation any license which has been suspended as provided by this subsection.
(4) The city commission must make its final determination within ten business days of the completion of the appeal hearing.
(b) Adverse licensure actions initiated by the city commission.
(1) In addition to the procedures provided in subsection (a), the city commission may, of its own volition, suspend, revoke, or not renew a license issued under this division following a hearing.
(2) A notice explaining the proposed adverse action, i.e. suspension, revocation, or non-renewal, and the time and place designated for the hearing must be issued to the licensee in writing.
(3) The written notice must set forth, in reasonable detail, the ground or grounds for the proposed adverse action and the factual basis supporting the ground or grounds; and advise the licensee of the right to present evidence, witnesses, and arguments and to be represented by counsel at the hearing.
(4) The hearing will not be held prior to the passage often days following the date of notice of the proposed adverse action.
(5) The city commission must make its final determination within ten business days of the completion of the hearing.
(6) The city commission's decision must be personally served, mailed by certified mail, return receipt requested, or by overnight delivery to the licensee and his attorney, with a copy to the city attorney, within ten business days of the close of the hearing.
(7) The decision of the city commission constitutes final action by the city, subject to review upon petition for certiorari to the Superior Court of Dade County, Georgia.
(c) Upon receipt of notice of adverse action against the licensee under this section, the licensee may waive its right to a hearing and stipulate to a sanction, as recommended by the city clerk in consultation with the chief of police. Any stipulation entered under this subsection shall be in writing, signed by the licensee, and is not appealable.
(d) Except as provided in subsection (a) of this section, no license will be suspended, revoked, or non-renewed without the opportunity for a hearing as provided in this section.

(a) No person shall be employed to dispense distilled spirits or serve in any managerial position by an establishment holding a license under this division until such person has been fingerprinted and cleared by the chief of police for the city or his designee or city code enforcement officer indicating that the person is eligible for such employment as per the minimum requirements for an applicant under this division.

(a) In addition to the license fees required in this division and in addition to the excise taxes levied by the state, there is hereby imposed an excise tax on the sale of distilled spirits.
(b) Excise taxes on the wholesale of distilled spirits. There is hereby levied an excise tax computed at the rate of $0.22 per liter which shall be paid to the city on all distilled spirits sold in the city. Such tax shall be paid to the city by the wholesaler on all distilled spirits sold to retail dealers in the city as follows:

(2) The $0.22 per liter rate shall be prorated so that all containers of distilled spirits shall be taxed on the basis of $0.22 per liter.

The governing authority of the City of Trenton, Georgia, pursuant to Article IX, Section 2, Paragraph 1 of the State of Georgia, hereby ordains and enacts into law the following ordinance.
This article shall be referred to and cited as the "City of Trenton Adult Entertainment Ordinance".
(Ord. of 1-3-2000, §§ 1.01, 1.02)
263:
The provisions of this article shall apply to all the incorporated areas of city and no business or establishment shall be undertaken, commenced or maintained without prior approval and authorization pursuant to the provisions herein.
(Ord. of 1-3-2000, § 1.03)
264:
This article is designed for various purposes including:
(1) To establish rules, regulations, procedures and standards for the licensing of adult entertainment establishments as defined herein.
(2) To foster and preserve the public health, safety, comfort and welfare, and to aid in the harmonious, orderly, aesthetically pleasing and socially beneficial development of the county.
(3) To regulate certain types of businesses, including but not limited to adult entertainment establishments, to the end that the many types of criminal activities frequently engendered by such businesses and the adverse affect on property values and on the public health, safety, and welfare of the city, and on its citizens and property, and on the character of its neighborhoods and development will be curtailed. This article is not intended as a de facto prohibition of legally protected forms of expression. This article is intended to represent a balancing of competing interests: reduced criminal activity and protection of neighborhoods and development through the regulation of adult entertainment establishments versus any legally protected rights of adult entertainment establishments and patrons. This article is not intended to allow or license any business, establishment, or activity, which would otherwise be unlawful.
(Ord. of 1-3-2000, § 1.04)
265:
The board of commissioners finds that many types of criminal activity may be engendered by the types of activities, which are regulated herein. These criminal activities are a drain on law enforcement resources. A consequential result of such criminal activity is the decline of our neighborhoods and a decline in property values. In looking to neighboring jurisdiction, we recognize the detrimental and deleterious effects brought about by these activities. The board finds it to be in the public interest to vigorously, within the bounds of the law, regulate and control adult entertainment establishments to avoid, to the extent possible, the undesirable consequences of such activities.
(Ord. of 1-3-2000, § 1.05)
266:
Any adult entertainment establishment operated, conducted or maintained contrary to the provisions of this article shall be and the same is hereby declared to be unlawful and a public nuisance. The city may, in addition to or in lieu of all other remedies, commence an action or actions, proceeding or proceedings for abatement, removal or enjoinment thereof, in the manner provided by law.
No adult entertainment establishment shall be conducted on any premises which do not comply with all zoning, building code, fire and other ordinances and laws of the city and the state or with any restrictive covenants that may apply to the property where it may be located.
(Ord. of 1-3-2000, § 1.06)
267:

(Ord. of 1-3-2000, § 1.07)
